- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the immediate next period; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 0.5–1.5% downward bias for 2–3 periods ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates in early periods when sentiment is positive; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shifts abruptly (e.g., from bullish to bearish), model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment change.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate; apply 1–2% upward bias to avoid “safety-first” underreaction.
